questions.stem: In the context of data, what does data deactivation refer to?
options: The intentional process of rendering certain data inactive by restricting access, archiving it or taking it out of active use
The permanent and irreversible destruction of all copies of a dataset
The encryption of data so that it can no longer be read by anyone
The migration of data from one database vendor to another
The automatic correction of errors found in a dataset
questions.explanation: Data deactivation is the intentional process of making data inactive, which involves restricting access, archiving it, or taking it out of active use.

questions.stem: When inactive customer records are archived under data deactivation, what happens to the data?
options: It is permanently deleted from all systems
It is made inactive but still retained for historical or compliance purposes
It is sold to third-party marketing companies
It is merged into the records of active customers
It is converted into anonymous statistics only
questions.explanation: Archiving inactive customer records makes the data inactive, but it is still retained for historical or compliance purposes.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of user account deactivation?
options: Resetting a customer's password after a forgotten-password request
Granting a new employee access to the finance system
Deactivating the account of an employee who has left the company so they can no longer access company data and systems
Backing up a user's mailbox before a server migration
Upgrading a user's licence to a premium tier
questions.explanation: When an employee leaves, their user account is deactivated, which prevents the former employee from accessing company data and systems.

questions.stem: Why might a web application temporarily deactivate certain features or services?
options: To increase the price of the service
To force users to create new accounts
To permanently retire the application
For maintenance or updates, during which certain data-related functionalities could be temporarily disabled
To comply with an embargo on international trade
questions.explanation: Temporary suspension for maintenance is one interpretation of data deactivation: features or services are deactivated during maintenance or updates.

questions.stem: What do data retention policies specify in relation to data deactivation?
options: Which users are allowed to create new records
How data should be encrypted during transmission
The format in which reports must be generated
Which programming language must be used for archiving
When certain types of data should be deactivated, archived or permanently deleted
questions.explanation: Data retention policies specify when certain types of data should be deactivated, archived, or permanently deleted, ensuring compliance and reducing storage costs.

questions.stem: In an e-commerce system, what is the effect of flagging products or services that are no longer offered as inactive?
options: Customers are prevented from making new purchases of those items
The items are automatically discounted to clear stock
Historical orders for those items are deleted
The items are moved to a competitor's catalogue
Suppliers are automatically notified to restock
questions.explanation: Disabling inactive products or services prevents customers from making new purchases of those items.

questions.stem: How might data deactivation be applied in response to a security incident?
options: By publishing all affected data so it can be reviewed publicly
By temporarily deactivating certain data access, such as suspending user accounts or restricting access to sensitive information
By deleting the entire database to remove the threat
By disabling all encryption to speed up investigation
By moving the data to an unmonitored server
questions.explanation: In the event of a security incident, certain data access might be temporarily deactivated to prevent unauthorised access, which could involve suspending user accounts or restricting access to sensitive information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the reasons given for archiving or disabling data through deactivation?
options: Compliance with data retention policies
Reducing the storage load
Retaining data for historical purposes
Preventing a former employee from accessing systems
Increasing the number of active user accounts
questions.explanation: Deactivation is done for reasons such as compliance with retention policies, reducing storage load, retaining data for history or compliance, and blocking access by former employees; increasing active accounts is not one of them.

questions.stem: Which interpretation of data deactivation refers to pausing certain data processing activities for maintenance, security or other reasons?
options: Permanent deletion
Data migration
Temporary suspension
Data replication
Schema redesign
questions.explanation: Temporary suspension refers to a temporary suspension or deactivation of certain data processing activities for maintenance, security, or other reasons.

questions.stem: In general terms, what does deactivation imply?
options: Copying something to a second location
Upgrading something to a newer version
Sharing something with a wider audience
The action of making something inactive or turning it off
Measuring how often something is used
questions.explanation: In general terms, deactivation implies the action of making something inactive or turning it off; in the data context it means intentionally rendering certain data inactive.
